comment: The shared Today tabs of docs/synchronisation.md §27 (card 507). Read by src/shared/ios-sync-today-contract.test.ts (played against src/shared/sync-today.ts and the merge of src/shared/sync-merge.ts) and by LuciumKit (SyncTodayVectorTests, against SyncToday.swift and SyncMerge.swift). Sections: limits; fieldClasses (the classes of todayTab, §27.2); address (§27.3 condition 3, §27.7); activeAt (§27.2, §27.5); admission (§27.3, §27.4: the conditions, the sticky admission, the cap; a case's `cap` replaces the 200 of `limits` so that a vector stays small); gate (the door of §27.4: invalid-url, invalid-value, too-many-today-tabs; a case's `limit` replaces the 500 of `limits`); moves (pinning and detaching, §27.2); merge (cases of the format of sync-merge-vectors.json: the conflicts of §27.9, the first exchange of §27.10, a locked space of §27.7; in `expect.order` a null means that the list is absent). The closing of a tab on the other device (an archive entry with the id of the tab, source sync, §27.5) is not here: it belongs to the cards that write the Mac and the phone.

address.name: 4097 bytes, fewer characters than the limit

admission.name: an ordinary tab, open for a minute, enters
a private tab does not enter
a tab of a private window does not enter
the page of a favourite does not enter
a tab of a container does not enter
a tab of a locked space does not enter
a script is not a web page
a file is not a web page
an address of 4097 bytes is left out, never cut
an address of 4096 bytes enters
a tab open for 19.999 s is of passage
a tab open for 20 s enters
sticky: a tab already admitted stays on an internal page
sticky: a tab already admitted stays on an address that is too long
sticky: a lock set later does not take the tab out (the merge sets the space aside)
sticky: a tab already admitted that became private is out
full: the most recently used take the places, then the id
full: a tab already admitted keeps its place and uses one
full: never a removal, the tabs already admitted stay above the cap
a place that is free is taken as soon as there is a tab for it
a tab refused for what it is does not take a place

gate.name: an entity that is in order passes as it is
a new entity carries its seeds, the address and the title
the fields of the class local are taken off, with their marks
a field this version does not know crosses (§11.6)
a script is refused, and the entity is dropped when the base does not hold it
a file address is refused: the base's version stands in, so that the gap is not read as a closing
an address of 4097 bytes is refused
an address that is not a text is refused
a title of more than 300 bytes is cut, on a boundary of characters
a title is cut without splitting a four-byte character
a title that is not a text is refused
an activeAt that is not a number is refused
too many: the best ranked are kept, newest first then the id (limit 3)
too many: an entity that is dropped and is in the base is given back as the base holds it
exactly the limit: nothing is refused

moves.name: pinning: todayTab/x removed and tab/x created is one move
detaching: tab/x removed and todayTab/x created is one move
a closing alone (or a pinning while structure is not common) is no move
an opening alone is no move
a pinned tab created while another id is removed is no move
a kind that is not a tab is no move

cases.name: closed here, navigated there: the closing wins (a navigation is no tracked field)
closed here, read there (activeAt later): the tab is kept
closed here, moved to another space there: the tab is kept, in that space
closed here, renamed there: the tab is kept, with its name
closed here, given an icon there: the tab is kept, with its icon
closed on both devices: absent, the greater tombstone is kept
first exchange, the same address on both devices: two tabs, no merge by address
first exchange: the union of both lists, ordered by birth then id, no conflict
first exchange, a phone never modified adopts the tabs of the Mac (its Today snapshot is empty)
renamed on both devices: the greater mark wins
reordered here, opened there: the reorder is kept and the new tab goes to the end
reordered on both devices: the list with the greater mark wins
pinned here, intact there: the tab changes list (todayTab removed, tab added)
pinned here, closed there: the tab comes back pinned on both devices
detached here, intact there: the tab changes list (tab removed, todayTab added)
no base: a tombstone removes the tab it is later than, and loses to a later change
read there, unchanged here: the later activeAt is taken, no conflict
a locked space is set aside: its Today tabs and their list are in no input and not in the result
a Today tab of a space that is not there is removed, and leaves a tombstone
a space deleted here, a Today tab moved into it there: the space is kept
